issues: Both quotes re-fetched and verbatim (--check FOUND).

'Hesse passed the first data protection statute of any kind in October 1970' is wrong on the month. The Hessian Landtag passed the act at its 80th sitting on 30 September 1970 (second and third readings, 'Gesetz beschlossen'); 7 October 1970 is the date it was signed, it was promulgated on 12 October and it came into force on 13 October. Primary evidence (scanned, no text layer, so --check is impossible; read visually from the page images): Hessischer Landtag, 6. Wahlperiode, Stenographischer Bericht Nr. 80, 80. Sitzung, Wiesbaden, 30 September 1970 (https://starweb.hessen.de/cache/PLPR/06/0/00080.pdf). Contents p. IV, item 14: 'Zweite und dritte Lesung des Entwurfs für ein Datenschutzgesetz - Drucks. Nr. 3065 und 3376 - In zweiter und dritter Lesung angenommen: Gesetz beschlossen'. p. 4272, President Buch: 'Das Gesetz ist mit den Stimmen der SPD, CDU und F.D.P. angenommen, ohne Gegenstimmen, bei Stimmenthaltung der NPD. Damit ist der Entwurf zum Gesetz erhoben.' The Gesetz- und Verordnungsblatt für das Land Hessen Teil I, 1970 Nr. 41 (https://starweb.hessen.de/cache/GVBL/1970/00041.pdf, also scanned) is 'Ausgegeben zu Wiesbaden am 12. Oktober 1970'; p. 625 reads 'Der Landtag hat das folgende Gesetz beschlossen: Datenschutzgesetz Vom 7. Oktober 1970'. The same issue lists nine laws all dated 7.10.70, several of which (Acetylenverordnung, Architektengesetz, Personalvertretungsgesetz, Schiedsmannsgesetz, Gerichtsorganisationsgesetz) were also passed at the 30 September sitting - so 7 October is the signing (Ausfertigung) date, not the vote.

'nearly three years earlier' overstates the gap: the Datalag (1973:289) was issued on 11 May 1973 (Riksdag open data: 'Utfärdad: 1973-05-11'), about two years and seven months after Hesse's act. Corrected to 'some two and a half years'. The riksdagen source is added.

'the first national data protection law' - the Swedish source's own claim is narrower: the first national law to regulate computerised processing of personal data comprehensively. The US Fair Credit Reporting Act (October 1970) was an earlier national but sectoral law. Wording tightened to 'first comprehensive national'.

fieldFixes.correction: Sweden's Datalag, issued on 11 May 1973, was the first comprehensive national data protection law. But the West German state of Hesse passed the first data protection statute of any kind in 1970, some two and a half years earlier, and elected the first data protection commissioner in June 1971.

issues: The record's correction is false. It says '30 September 1970 was a reading of the bill'. In fact 30 September 1970 was the day the Hessian Landtag passed the act, in its second and third readings, with no votes against. Primary evidence (scanned, no text layer, so --check is impossible; read visually from the page images): Hessischer Landtag, 6. Wahlperiode, Stenographischer Bericht Nr. 80, 80. Sitzung, Wiesbaden, 30 September 1970 (https://starweb.hessen.de/cache/PLPR/06/0/00080.pdf). Contents p. IV, item 14: 'Zweite und dritte Lesung des Entwurfs für ein Datenschutzgesetz - Drucks. Nr. 3065 und 3376 - In zweiter und dritter Lesung angenommen: Gesetz beschlossen'. p. 4272, President Buch: 'Das Gesetz ist mit den Stimmen der SPD, CDU und F.D.P. angenommen, ohne Gegenstimmen, bei Stimmenthaltung der NPD. Damit ist der Entwurf zum Gesetz erhoben.' The Gesetz- und Verordnungsblatt für das Land Hessen Teil I, 1970 Nr. 41 (https://starweb.hessen.de/cache/GVBL/1970/00041.pdf, also scanned) is 'Ausgegeben zu Wiesbaden am 12. Oktober 1970'; p. 625 reads 'Der Landtag hat das folgende Gesetz beschlossen: Datenschutzgesetz Vom 7. Oktober 1970'. The same issue lists nine laws all dated 7.10.70, several of which (Acetylenverordnung, Architektengesetz, Personalvertretungsgesetz, Schiedsmannsgesetz, Gerichtsorganisationsgesetz) were also passed at the 30 September sitting - so 7 October is the signing (Ausfertigung) date, not the vote.

So the 'myth' claim ('Hesse enacted the world's first data protection law on 30 September 1970') is essentially true if 'enacted' means the legislature's vote, which is how the BfDI uses 'erlässt'. It is only imprecise because the act's official date is 7 October 1970 (the signature date, which gives the law its name) and it came into force on 13 October 1970. A record that brands the BfDI's date an error, while treating the archive's '7 October ... verabschiedete der Hessische Landtag' as right, gets the facts backwards.

Source 2 (Arcinsys) is quoted verbatim, but its statement is itself inaccurate: the Landtag did not vote on 7 October. It passed the act on 30 September; 7 October is the Ausfertigung date. Any other record relying on this Arcinsys sentence for 'the Landtag passed it on 7 October' should be corrected. That includes the source note on event hesse-data-protection-act-1970, which translates it as 'On 7 October 1970 the Hessian Landtag passed the Data Protection Act' (outside this chunk). The slice 'notes' pointer to this myth should also be removed.

If editors want a date-clarifying item in its place, a true version would read: 'Hesse's Landtag passed the act on 30 September 1970, with no votes against. It is dated 7 October 1970, the day it was signed, was published in the Gesetz- und Verordnungsblatt on 12 October and came into force on 13 October 1970, so sources that give either 30 September or 7 October are both right about different steps.' This is a nuance, not a myth.

It does not say which reading was the final vote; the plenary record shows 30 September was the second and third reading, when the act was passed.

fieldFixes.correction: The 1973 HEW report proposed legally enforceable 'safeguard requirements', with violations treated as an 'unfair information practice' carrying criminal penalties and civil remedies, and wrote that when privacy is traded for a benefit 'both parties to the exchange should participate in setting the terms'. The Justice Department's account says the authors rejected a property-based model of individual control in favour of a governance framework meant to earn the trust of everyone with a stake in the information, individuals and agencies alike. Notice-and-choice as practised online came later.
